title: Cohesion without formula
summary: Connect sentences through clear reference, logical sequence, controlled repetition and selective transitions so that relationships—not stock linking phrases—guide the reader.

sections.title: Cohesion is a path, not a pile of connectors
content: E7.1 gave each paragraph one promise, and E7.2 developed that promise with purposeful specifics. Cohesion now makes the relationship between those ideas easy to follow. It is not created by adding ‘firstly’, ‘secondly’ and ‘furthermore’ to every sentence.
A cohesive paragraph lets the reader answer three questions without guessing: What does this sentence refer to? How does it relate to the previous idea? What new information should I carry forward?

sections.title: Move from given information to new information
content: A useful sentence pattern is given to new: begin from an idea the reader already knows, then add the next important detail. ‘The checklist exposed an unconfirmed drinks order. That missing order became the group’s next priority.’ The reference ‘that missing order’ picks up known information before the sentence advances to the decision.

The pattern is flexible, not a rule for every sentence. Use it when the reader needs a bridge. If several sentences begin with unrelated new topics, the paragraph may feel like a list even when each sentence is grammatically correct.

sections.title: Build an unmistakable reference chain
content: Repeat the key noun when a new stage begins, then vary it only when the referent remains certain: ‘water approached the extension lead. The approaching water created a safety risk. That risk changed the order of the move.’ Strategic repetition is clearer than replacing every noun with a decorative synonym.

Check pronouns and pointing words such as ‘it’, ‘they’, ‘this’ and ‘that’. ‘This changed everything’ is weak when ‘this’ could mean either the rain or the water near the cable. Name the idea—‘This safety risk’—when two possible referents compete.

sections.title: Let the relationship choose the transition
content: Transitions should reveal a real relationship. Use time links when events move forward, cause-and-consequence links when one fact produces another, contrast links when an expectation changes, and qualification when a claim needs limits. If no transition is needed, a clear reference chain may be enough.

Compare ‘Furthermore, water approached the lead’ with ‘When rainwater approached the lead, the group moved electrical equipment first.’ The second version names both time and cause. The first merely adds another fact and hides the reason for the decision.

sections.title: Choose a logical route for the paragraph
content: A paragraph may move through chronological sequence, cause to effect, problem to response, or general claim to specific evidence. Choose the route that fulfils its promise. The rain paragraph works as problem to response: the move exposed an electrical risk, the group changed priorities, and the controlled response demonstrated adaptation.

Keep thread words connected to that route: ‘step-by-step method’, ‘one priority at a time’ and ‘clear next action’ develop one concept. Random synonym swapping—calling the method a scheme, trick and magic—creates drift rather than variety.

sections.title: Repair the broken relationship
content: Classify cohesion problems as connector stacking, empty ordering, unclear reference, sudden topic jump, synonym drift or a missing logical step. Do not repair every problem by inserting another linking word. Repair the relationship itself: identify the referent, restore the missing cause or consequence, reorder the ideas, or remove the jump.
Read the paragraph once using only its reference chain and once using only its sequence of actions and consequences. If either route breaks, revise that break before polishing individual transitions.

sections.title: Make every connection earn its place
content: Make six decisions about given-to-new order, reference chains, logical relationships, selective transitions, thread words and missing steps. Complete the group before viewing feedback.
